decisions.reason: It is close to the firm's established pharmaceutical range, and with in-house R&D and formulation know-how the firm is well placed to learn from initial market feedback and improve it rather than withdraw it.

As a distant product in a generic segment that is less central to the firm's differentiated strategy, it is harder for management to interpret results and justify continued resource commitment despite the firm's general technical capabilities.
This product is close to the firm's existing offer and fits its manufacturing, formulation, and pharmacy-market capabilities, so absorptive capacity arguments favor retaining and developing it.

It builds directly on the firm's supplements and self-care business and supports the stated strategy of expanding differentiated pharmacy-oriented health products, even if its website presence suggests a somewhat lighter launch.
